rationale: Turns the last open half of the trim child's gap from a source reading into an executed observation. The harness gains one case, memory_storage_below_trimmed_request, which drives the shipped in-memory storage directly through the public Storage trait - append four entries, sample the initial length, trim past the second entry, then ask for a suffix and a range below the trimmed index under separate panic guards, and finally read at the trimmed index itself - so that the question the gap asks (a request below a compacted index: panic or silently empty suffix?) is answered by an observation for this implementation and build profile rather than only by the unguarded subtractions in memory_storage.rs. The case reports the length after the trim, both panic flags and the read at the trimmed index, and the experiment is a successor of the trim child's own experiment so the receipt lands in that investigation. No other record changed this update: the accounts are current, and each already states that this half of the gap rests on source reading until an execution covers it, which this run now will.

experiment.revision_reason: Adds the storage-level case memory_storage_below_trimmed_request, which drives MemoryStorage directly through the public Storage trait: append four entries, trim two, then read below and at the trimmed index under panic guards. Every previously generated case is unchanged apart from sharing one execution.

scope.description: The generated test file plus one storage-level case over a single MemoryStorage instance in the same process; the case bypasses the protocol entirely and calls the storage trait's own append, trim, get_suffix and get_entries methods, reporting any panic as an event field rather than aborting the run.
assumptions: Entry type Value has Snapshot = NoSnapshot and is used as the storage's entry type, as in the rest of the harness.

Four entries are appended and two are trimmed, so a request below the trimmed index means an index of 0 or 1 while the trimmed index is 2; the case reads the storage's log length before and after the trim as the observable of the trim itself.
Panics are caught with catch_unwind around each storage call, so the build's overflow-check setting decides whether the unguarded subtraction panics and the run continues either way.
excluded: No cluster, no protocol messages and no snapshot path are exercised in the new case; it is a storage-level probe only.
Only the shipped in-memory storage is exercised; no other implementation of the Storage trait is available in this tree.
No crate or package test suite is executed; only the generated test file.

experiment.prefix: The new case starts from an empty MemoryStorage, appends four values, emits STORPROBE_BASE with the log length, trims two entries, then calls get_suffix(1) and get_entries(0, 1) each inside catch_unwind, calls get_suffix(2) at the trimmed index, and emits STORPROBE_RESULT with the log length, the two panic flags and the state and length of the read at the trimmed index. The lineage cases that share the execution are unchanged.
semantic_changes: Adds the storage-level case memory_storage_below_trimmed_request; every previously generated case is unchanged apart from sharing one execution.

comparisons.description: A read below the trimmed index is reported or refused rather than aborting the caller, which is what the unguarded subtraction in the shipped in-memory storage would contradict.
The read at the trimmed index itself succeeds, so the probe distinguishes a below-trimmed request from an ordinary one.
